title: config.toml in Depth
description: One resolver folds defaults, user config, trusted project config, the selected profile, and CLI overrides into a single effective Config.

steps.content: sources (low -> high precedence): built-in defaults < ~/.codex/config.toml < .codex/config.toml (trusted) < --profile < -c key=value / flags
steps.annotation: Codex layers configuration from several sources; the later a source, the higher its precedence.
The user-level file sets the baseline for every session on this machine.
A trusted project may override non-sensitive keys; provider, auth, profile, and telemetry keys are ignored here.
A profile is a named overlay; model_providers.<id>.wire_api selects the wire protocol ("responses").

steps.content: resolve precedence: CLI / -c  >  --profile  >  project (trusted)  >  user  >  defaults
steps.annotation: A single resolver walks the layers from lowest to highest and lets each override the last.

steps.content: effective Config = { model:"gpt-5-codex", reasoning_effort:"high", approval_policy:"on-request", sandbox_mode:"workspace-write", network_access:true, wire_api:"responses" }
steps.annotation: The agent loop reads only the resolved Config; it never re-opens the raw files at run time.

steps.content: Running under the resolved policy: on-request approvals, workspace-write sandbox, network on.
steps.annotation: Every tool call in the loop is gated by the one effective Config.
The command executes inside the resolved sandbox; approval comes from the resolved approval_policy.
The loop proceeds under a single, deterministic configuration.
